# task-2e5d2205: offset boundary segments and marker-driven fills

## Recurrence evidence

The task has appeared with rectangular grids whose background is interrupted by two separated segments of a frame/boundary color, plus sparse single cells of a marker color. Do not interpret this as a generic diagonal-periodic fill. The frame segments and marker positions specify parallel bands/rays. Sparse marker cells become color 4, and marker color fills along the row toward the nearby frame segment. A marker also induces a full-width fill in the corresponding row of the opposite boundary-defined region, matching the relative offset within the paired segments.

## Accepted instance

Test `task-2e5d2205` (20x23): background 6; color-9 boundary segments at column 0, rows 0–5, and column 22, rows 10–15; one color-8 marker at `(row 14, col 6)` (zero-indexed). Accepted output preserved the 9 segments; changed marker `(14,6)` to 4; filled row 14, columns 7–21 with 8; and filled the corresponding offset row 4, columns 1–21 with 8. All other cells remained unchanged. This is a zero-error accepted reference.

## Demonstration patterns

- 30x8 demo: color-2 segments at right edge rows 0–13 and left edge rows 14–27; sparse color-1 markers in the second segment's span. Each marker row was filled from the marker toward the left boundary, marker became 4; the corresponding row in the first span was filled across the interior (columns 0–6) in color 1. Unmarked rows stayed background. This supports matching rows by relative offset between paired segments.
- 18x6 demo: color-7 short horizontal segments at top and bottom, with color-3 markers; output filled the aligned interior strip at columns 0–1 in color 3 and changed the marker cells to 4. This indicates orientation can rotate with boundary-segment arrangement; infer the fill axis and paired offsets from the observed geometry rather than assuming vertical segments.

## Procedure

1. Identify background, repeated boundary color, and sparse marker color; locate the two disconnected boundary segments.
2. Determine their relative alignment and span. Treat corresponding positions in the two segments as paired offsets.
3. For each marker, infer its associated segment and corresponding position in the paired segment. Fill from the marker toward the nearby boundary along the relevant axis in marker color, replacing the marker itself with 4.
4. Transfer the marker's influence to the paired region: fill the full interior cross-section at the corresponding offset with the marker color, stopping at the boundary. Leave rows/columns with no marker unchanged unless demos establish otherwise.
5. Preserve boundary segments and verify dimensions/serialization exactly.

## Caution

Only two demonstrations and one accepted test establish this family. Confirm orientation and offset interpretation on each fresh grid; do not assume a fixed color palette, boundary side, segment length, or axis. A single marker may trigger both its local ray and the corresponding cross-region stripe."
}
